ds: Indicators that the institution's own control environment may be weakened, increasing residual exposure to financial crime. Covers governance, alert backlogs, tuning gaps, insider risk, data quality and outsourcing. Intended for the control-effectiveness side of an enterprise-wide risk assessment.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Bank control-environment weaknesses.

rat: Institution's own control environment; not an exposure of a channel, rail, segment or product.

ind.cx: Board and senior management receive limited or irregular financial crime reporting and there is unclear accountability.
ind.fp: Small firms may have lean but effective governance.
ind.ds: Board and senior management receive limited or irregular financial crime reporting and there is unclear accountability.

ind.cx: Monitoring or screening alerts stay unreviewed beyond service levels.
ind.ds: Monitoring or screening alerts stay unreviewed beyond service levels.

ind.n: Monitoring scenarios not tuned or validated
ind.cx: Rules and models have not been calibrated, tested or reviewed against current risk.
ind.fp: Stable portfolios may need little change.
ind.ds: Rules and models have not been calibrated, tested or reviewed against current risk.

ind.n: Staff collusion or insider risk indicators
ind.cx: Employees show unusual relationships with customers, override controls or access records without need.
ind.ds: Employees override approvals, alter records, access records without need or show unusual relationships with customers.
ind.cn: Staff override of controls or excessive record access

ind.n: Poor customer and transaction data quality
ind.cx: Missing, inconsistent or incorrectly mapped data weakens screening and monitoring.
ind.ds: Missing, inconsistent or incorrectly mapped data weakens screening and monitoring.

ind.cx: Screening, onboarding or investigation tasks are outsourced with limited oversight.
ind.ds: Screening, onboarding or investigation tasks are outsourced with limited oversight.

ind.n: Overdue periodic reviews or KYC refresh
ind.cx: Customer reviews exceed scheduled dates, particularly for high-risk customers.
ind.ds: Customer reviews exceed scheduled dates, particularly for high-risk customers.

ind.n: Inadequate or outdated enterprise risk assessment
ind.cx: Risk assessment is stale, unscoped, or not used to drive controls.
ind.ds: Risk assessment is stale, unscoped, or not used to drive controls.

ind.n: Insufficient training or low staff awareness
ind.cx: Staff cannot recognise red flags, late completion of training, high error rates in quality checks.
ind.ds: Staff cannot recognise red flags, late completion of training, high error rates in quality checks.

ind.n: Slow or poor-quality suspicious activity reporting
ind.cx: Reports are filed late, are thin in content or the volume is out of line with peers.
ind.ds: Reports are filed late, are thin in content or the volume is out of line with peers.

ind.cx: Previous findings remain open or recur.
ind.fp: Remediation can be long-running by design.
ind.ds: Previous findings remain open or recur.

ctl.ds: Performs and refreshes a documented assessment of inherent risk, controls and residual risk across customers, products, channels, geographies and sectors, and links risks to specific controls and gaps. It directs resources and shapes policy.
Reports control performance indicators, backlogs and issues to senior management and the board on a regular cycle for challenge and decision. It keeps risk acceptance and resourcing visible.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.
Documents roles, ownership and escalation for first-line, compliance and independent assurance responsibilities for financial crime controls. Clear accountability reduces gaps and duplication.
Tracks alert, review and case ageing against service levels, triages by risk and adds capacity or remediation programmes to clear backlogs. It prevents delay from eroding control effectiveness.

ctl.n: Suspicious reporting timeliness and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Measures how quickly suspicious activity reports are filed after suspicion forms and subjects narratives to peer or second-line review for completeness and usefulness. Weak or late reports are corrected and root causes fed back to analysts, so intelligence reaches authorities on time and in a usable form.

ctl.n: Scenario tuning and independent model validation
ctl.ds: Periodically tests thresholds, coverage and segmentation, including above and below the line, and independently validates scenarios and models with documented rationale for changes. It keeps detection effective and defensible.

Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.
Restricts and logs privileged and bulk access to customer and case systems and alerts on anomalous user activity. It deters insider misuse and leakage of sensitive investigations and customer data.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.

Measures completeness, accuracy and timeliness of the data that feeds screening and monitoring, reconciles sources and assigns named owners and deadlines for remediation. Controls built on poor data fail silently, so this keeps detection reliable.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

Contracts service levels, quality standards and audit rights with vendors performing control activities, and samples their outputs for accuracy. It keeps outsourced screening, monitoring or onboarding to the institution's own standard.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Assigns each customer a risk tier from factors such as customer type, sector, geography, products and channel, which then drives the depth of due diligence and monitoring. Consistent scoring focuses resources on higher-risk relationships.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.
Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.

Records control issues with owners and deadlines, escalates overdue items and independently confirms that remediation has worked before closure. It ensures weaknesses are fixed rather than merely logged.
